title: Rings upon rings
caption: The barred spiral galaxy Messier 95, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Messier 95 · constellation Leo · about 35 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble portrait shows Messier 95 (M95, or NGC 3351), about 35 million light-years away in the constellation Leo (The Lion). It is a barred spiral galaxy. A bar of stars cuts through its center and is ringed by an inner ring where new stars are forming.

Pierre Méchain discovered the galaxy in 1781, and Charles Messier cataloged it just four days later. Messier mainly hunted comets and was often annoyed by objects that looked like comets but were not, so he built his catalog to help others avoid the same confusion.

Messier 95 has also hosted a supernova, the explosive end of a massive star. SN 2012aw appeared in the outer part of one of its spiral arms. Once its light faded, astronomers compared images from before and after the explosion to find which star had vanished. It was a red supergiant up to 26 times as massive as the Sun.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.71 x 2.53 arcminutes) and distance (35 million light years), the frame spans roughly 28,000 × 26,000 light-years. Its light set out about 35 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 observed Messier 95 in ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: Some of these filters record ultraviolet and near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and the galaxy is far too faint for unaided eyes.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture was made with Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 through five filters, from ultraviolet to near-infrared light. Like Messier 95, our own Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy, with a bar of stars running through its center.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with a bar through its center surrounded by an inner ring of star formation.
